harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created a "Fleet Internal CA" root CA on node1, issued a TLS server certificate for node2 (CN=node2, SAN=DNS:node2,IP:10.100.162.11) signed by that CA, deployed the cert/key to node2 and configured nginx to serve HTTPS on port 8443. Installed the CA certificate as a trusted system anchor (update-ca-trust) on both node1 and node2. Verified full chain trust via curl using each node's default OS trust store (no --cacert override needed) and via openssl s_client. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol for both nodes with boot-id proof and post-restart re-verification of CA trust, cert files, nginx service, and HTTPS reachability.
actions_performed: Inspected both nodes (AlmaLinux 9, root, openssl present)
Built CA directory structure on node1
Generated 4096-bit CA key and self-signed X.509 CA cert CN=Fleet Internal CA, 10-year validity
Generated node2 key/CSR with SAN (DNS:node2, IP:10.100.162.11) and signed it with the Fleet Internal CA; verified chain with openssl verify
Set up passwordless SSH between nodes using the cluster keypair
Installed nginx on node2
Transferred node2 cert/key/CA cert from node1 to node2 via scp and set correct file permissions/ownership
Configured nginx TLS server block on port 8443 using the issued cert/key; validated config, enabled and started the service, opened firewall port 8443/tcp
Verified HTTPS on node2:8443 from node1 using explicit CA file, then again using each node's default system trust store after installing the CA
Installed the Fleet Internal CA certificate as a trusted system anchor via update-ca-trust on both node1 and node2 and confirmed via `trust list`
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, uptime, service/trust state) on both nodes

Restarted node1 via systemctl reboot (backgrounded so ack returned before disconnect), polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, and re-verified CA trust anchor, CA files, and TLS reachability to node2

Restarted node2 via systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, and re-verified nginx active, port 8443 listening, cert files intact, CA trust anchor present, and HTTPS response
Final cross-check from node1 confirming end-to-end HTTPS trust chain after both restarts

evidence.requirement: CA 'Fleet Internal CA' created on node1
evidence.summary: CA directory initialized and 4096-bit self-signed CA certificate generated with CN=Fleet Internal CA, CA:TRUE basic constraint

evidence.requirement: TLS certificate issued for node2 by the Fleet Internal CA
evidence.summary: node2 key/CSR generated with SAN DNS:node2,IP:10.100.162.11, signed by CA, openssl verify returns OK, and SAN confirmed in issued cert text

evidence.requirement: node2 serves HTTPS on port 8443 with the issued certificate
evidence.summary: nginx configured with ssl_certificate/ssl_certificate_key pointing at the issued cert, listening on 0.0.0.0:8443, and curl from node1 with --cacert against the CA succeeds with TLS 1.3 and SSL certificate verify ok

evidence.requirement: CA installed as trusted system CA on node1
evidence.summary: CA cert copied to /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors, update-ca-trust extract run, trust list shows Fleet Internal CA as anchor/authority, and curl to node2:8443 without --cacert succeeds using default system trust store plus openssl s_client verify return code 0

evidence.requirement: CA installed as trusted system CA on node2
evidence.summary: CA cert copied to /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors on node2, update-ca-trust extract run, trust list shows Fleet Internal CA as anchor, and local curl to its own HTTPS endpoint succeeds

evidence.requirement: node1 restart evidence: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 5fb1b173... captured; systemctl reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; subsequent calls failed (connection reset/timeout) proving the node went down; node came back with new boot_id 10d8b6c3... and new uptime start; post-restart checks confirm CA trust anchor present, CA key/cert files intact, and node2's HTTPS service still verifiable from node1

evidence.requirement: node2 restart evidence: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id d6298ced... and healthy nginx/HTTPS captured; systemctl reboot acknowledged; subsequent call still showed old boot_id then a following call timed out (connection lost) confirming reboot in progress; node came back with new boot_id 291eaef8... and new uptime start; post-restart checks confirm nginx active, port 8443 listening, cert files intact, CA trust anchor present, local HTTPS working, and cross-node HTTPS verification from node1 with full chain trust (Verify return code: 0)
